inForce.basis: A summary, not law: its own period statement is the only currency signal. It also says 'For in-season regulation changes visit www.gov.bc.ca/hunting', which was not checked.

statedAs.text: Licences are available online at www.gov.bc.ca/hunting and at Service BC, FrontCounter BC and participating commercial outlets and sporting goods stores.

obtain.note: If you buy your species licence online, it will be mailed to you and it is subject to Canada Post delivery times.

statedAs.text: Upland Game Birds No Species licence required $50.00

unresolved: The table's text layer prints the resident cell 'No Species licence required' and the non-resident cell '$50.00'. B.C. Reg. 8/99 Schedule item 2.5 gives 35.00 + 15.00 = 50.00, and s. 5 (3) requires it of 'a non-resident or non-resident alien'. The condition statedAs is our description of the column, not a sentence: the source has none.

geography.statedAs: Restricted to private land only, hunter must obtain permission from landowners prior to access.

unresolved: TIER: this sentence is the Synopsis (OFFICIAL_SUMMARY), not law. The governing provision, B.C. Reg. 190/84 Schedule 4 Part 2 s. 21, says only 'on private property' and says nothing about permission. Do not present the permission requirement as a regulation; if shown, attribute it to the ministry's Synopsis. Trespass law (not read) may independently require permission.

researchNotes: Text layer extracted with pypdf; two-column pages interleave, so only sentences verified contiguous in the extracted text are quoted. Requirements are sourced from LAW-tier packages; this package supplies obtain channels and a fee cross-check only.
The Synopsis introduction states the proposed lead-shot prohibition 'was put on hold'; the upland-bird ammunition rows therefore rest on B.C. Reg. 190/84 s. 17 alone.
